name: Resignation
overview: The Scriptures reveal resignation as a posture of humble acceptance of God's sovereign will, even amid loss or discipline. For example, Genesis 43:14 reflects a willingness to endure bereavement as part of God's providence, while Aaron's silent submission after the death of his sons in Leviticus 10:3 exemplifies reverent acceptance of divine holiness and justice. Similarly, the Israelites' confession in Judges 10:15 and Samuel's acknowledgment in 1 Samuel 3:18 demonstrate a trust that God will act justly and wisely according to His purposes. These passages collectively teach that resignation involves trusting God's faithfulness and goodness, even when His ways are difficult to understand.
